name: Glen Industries Ltd
tagline: ~22% growth in a sustainable-packaging niche (PLA/paper straws, thin-wall containers), but D/E ~2.9, an independent 'weak quality' flag and BSE-SME liquidity keep conviction Low
business_overview: Glen Industries (BSE SME, 544444; originally Glen Stationery, 2007) manufactures food packaging and service products — thin-wall food containers, polylactic-acid (PLA) straws and paper straws — for HoReCa, QSR, food & beverage and dairy customers. Listed on BSE SME in July 2025. No usable ValuePickr thread found; web/news + old-project baseline only.
fundamentals_table: ~16.6% / ~13.8% (some sources show higher on different periods)
~22% revenue CAGR; Q1 FY27 revenue +24.4% YoY (domestic +43.8%, exports -15.3%)
Net debt ~Rs 87 Cr (down from ~Rs 129 Cr); D/E ~2.9 — elevated for an SME
fundamentals_narrative: Real growth (~22% revenue CAGR, Q1 FY27 +24.4%) in a structurally supported niche (single-use-plastic bans driving PLA/paper straw demand). But leverage is high for an SME (D/E ~2.9, net debt ~Rs 87 Cr), an independent quality screen flagged 'weak quality' on an inconsistent multi-year track record, exports softened in Q1 FY27 (-15.3%), and the stock is well below its listing-day pop. Listed only July 2025.

verdict_headline: Real growth and a genuine packaging tailwind keep it in the 10x frame, but leverage, a quality flag and SME liquidity hold conviction to Low
verdict_reasoning: ~22% revenue CAGR, a Q1 FY27 domestic acceleration and a structural sustainable-packaging tailwind at a ~Rs 274 Cr base support a 10x-in-2-3-years framing
Conviction is Low: D/E ~2.9 is elevated for an SME, an independent screen flags inconsistent quality, exports are soft, and there is no community validation

four_box.note: Verdict explicit 'structural sustainable-packaging tailwind' (yes); independent screen flags inconsistent quality (moat weak); D/E~2.9 elevated; no tam/valuation detail.

quality_metrics.note: SME IPO Jul 2025. ROCE 14% FY26 vs 23% 3-yr avg; OPM contracted 24%->19%, PAT down YoY (Rs18cr->Rs16cr). Borrowings rose to Rs121cr vs ~Rs38cr EBITDA (~3.2x); FY26 CFO only Rs6cr, FCF -Rs14cr (~-37% conversion) as PLA/paper-straw + thin-wall capacity ramps. Single-use-plastic-ban tailwind is real but leverage, negative FCF and margin contraction are live concerns.
